Where the male line's oldest documented man died. Not a family place — a trap. Booysens is a mining suburb south of the Johannesburg city centre, a couple of miles from Forest Hill and Kenilworth where this family actually lived in the 1940s. The farm where the oldest document in this archive was written. Fifteen years later it takes two more: his son's wife on 9 May 1891 and their son five days after her. Where this family's western Transvaal branch is, and it is a branch rather than a lead now. Lichtenburg is one district west of Rustenburg, where his father died in 1876, and one district east of Marico.

Where a Booyzen worked underground. The Indwe marriage register of 21 September 1908 gives both bride and groom's dwelling place as “Dugmore Mijn” and the groom's trade as “Mijnwerker”. The coordinates are approximate — the workings were at Indwe and the exact site is not yet fixed.

One farm, two deaths, thirty-five years apart, and the same family on it both times. Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus Booijsen — born district Graaff-Reinet about 1818, fifth child on the 1876 Sterfkennis — died here on 25 May 1885. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria, born about 1860, died here on 1 May 1920. It is the clearest evidence this archive has that the family did not merely pass through the western Transvaal but settled in it, two generations before anyone reached Johannesburg. The coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed.

The third named Barry farm, after Manorowen and Jerpoint. Harriet Louisa Barry, eighteen, died here of typhoid on 7 September 1912 after thirty days' illness and was carried back to Manorowen to be buried.
